title: SLO Artifact Lineage and Rollout Accountability Map
creator: Asha Ramesh
body:
Problem: As we scale SLO-driven reliability work across Hosted, Dedicated and Private customers, it's increasingly hard to trace the lifecycle of an SLO from definition to alerting, runbooks, dashboards, ownership changes, and rollout gates. This leads to gaps during releases (unsynced dashboards, stale runbooks), unclear rollback ownership, and difficulty forecasting error-budget impacts across initiatives.

Goal: Create a single SLO artifact lineage model and an accompanying accountability map that ties SLO config (service + objective), SLI measurement code, alert rules, dashboard panels, runbooks, rollout gates, and initiative tickets to named owners and automated trace links. The deliverable is a living JSON-backed registry + onboarding checklist + runbook that product, SRE, and engineering teams can use when creating or changing SLOs.

Scope: Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated control plane, and Private deploy control plane SLOs. Excludes model-level quality SLOs (evaluations); those are tracked by Applied ML.

Outcomes: 1) Reduce incident TTR from incomplete runbooks and missing owner handoffs, 2) Decrease rollouts that require emergency rollbacks due to telemetry mismatches, 3) Make initiative-level error budget forecasts accurate to within 15% of observed burn within one month of rollout.

High-level approach: 1) Define an SLO artifact schema (flat key-value fields to support Linear/GitHub/Confluence links), 2) Implement a lightweight registry (initially a repo + CLI + automated CI validation) that validates referenced artifacts exist, 3) Populate the registry for existing high-priority SLOs, 4) Add an onboarding checklist and a one-page rollout accountability map that must be attached to PM initiative tickets as a release gating requirement.

Acceptance criteria: - Schema defined and documented in the repo README with examples for Hosted/Dedicated/Private SLOs. - CI validation verifies all referenced artifacts (dashboard panels, runbooks, alert IDs) return 200 or exist in configured services. - Registry seeded with top-25 production SLOs and owners assigned. - Linear release gating template updated to require link to SLO registry entry for any initiative that touches capacity/latency/availability. - On-call runbooks reference the registry ID and have last-reviewed metadata within 180 days. - Rollout accountability map template used in two pilot initiatives and retro captured.

Acceptance tests / verification: - Run CI validation against seeded SLOs; failures must be <5% and resolved. - Pilot initiative 1: Dedicated autoscaler change — verify prerelease checklist prevents rollout when dashboard metric mismatch is detected. - Pilot initiative 2: KV-cache kernel change — measure error-budget forecasting accuracy after 30 days.

Tasks (initial):
1) Draft SLO artifact schema and example entries (PM + SRE)
2) Implement repo layout and CI check scripts (Engineering)
3) Create Linear release gating template and update PRD templates (PM)
4) Seed registry for top-25 SLOs and validate links (SRE + Eng + PM)
5) Run two cross-team pilots and capture retros (PM)
6) Publish onboarding checklist and 1-page accountability map (PM + Documentation)

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: Teams resist required gating — Mitigation: pilot with high-impact initiatives first and collect time-saved evidence; make gating incremental. - Risk: False negatives from CI checks (third-party dashboards blocked) — Mitigation: add allowlist and manual verification flow. - Risk: Ownership churn causes stale entries — Mitigation: add auto-reminder to owners and require review before major releases.

Communication plan: Announcement to Platform and Product channels, demo in weekly reliability sync, include short checklist and How-To doc in Console release notes.

Links and artifacts: (placeholders for repo/PRD/Dashboards will be populated during implementation)
